title: Admin: add per-tenant KMS health summary endpoint (sanitized)
author: Diego Santos
release_notes: Adds a new admin-only endpoint for summarizing per-tenant KMS health (sanitized) to speed up triage of KMS brownouts/rotation issues without exposing key material or customer identifiers.
body:
Context: As part of the KMS hardening work (ENG-4239 + ongoing rotation/testing), ops and on-call have repeatedly needed a fast way to answer “is KMS broken for this tenant, and if so, how?” without spelunking through logs or asking Security for raw key IDs. This PR adds an admin-only, sanitized per-tenant KMS health summary endpoint surfaced from the control plane, backed by data-plane emitted metrics/events already flowing through the audit/telemetry pipeline.

What’s included: (1) New endpoint: GET /admin/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/kms/health-summary. (2) RBAC gating: requires admin role + explicit permission kms.health.read (policy engine enforced; no fallback to legacy “support_read” role). (3) Sanitization: response does NOT include full KMS key ARNs, key aliases, ciphertext, request IDs, or customer-provided key policy text. Key identifiers are replaced with stable, non-reversible fingerprints (HMAC-SHA256 with server-side secret) and truncated to 12 chars; region/provider are allowed. Tenant name is not returned; caller must already know tenant_id. (4) Signal sources: last_successful_encrypt_at / last_successful_decrypt_at, last_error_at, last_error_class (Timeout/Throttling/AccessDenied/DisabledKey/Unknown), rolling error rate (5m/1h), p95 latency (5m), circuit breaker state (open/half-open/closed), cache hit ratio (prefix/KV crypto cache), and “active_key_fingerprint” + “previous_key_fingerprint” when dual-read rotation window is enabled. (5) SRE friendliness: includes a “recommended_next_steps” field with short, deterministic hints keyed off error_class + breaker state (e.g., “check IAM deny in CloudTrail / key policy”, “throttling: consider raising backoff ceiling; see runbook section 3.2”). (6) Audit logging: access to the endpoint emits an AUDIT_ADMIN_READ event with actor, tenant_id, and purpose field (required query param purpose=incident|support|testing); purpose is validated and logged.

Not included / intentionally excluded: (a) No per-request KMS diagnostics, no raw error messages from providers (these often contain resource names). (b) No endpoint in the public API or tenant-scoped console; this is admin-only for now. (c) No mutation operations (no “rotate now” or “toggle breaker”)—this is read-only by design.

Implementation notes: Control plane hosts the endpoint and fetches pre-aggregated health stats from the internal telemetry store keyed by tenant_id and provider. Data-plane already emits the underlying metrics; this PR adds a lightweight aggregation job and a cache layer (30s TTL) to keep the endpoint cheap during incidents. The policy check is enforced at the router (authz middleware) and again inside the handler as defense in depth.

Testing: Unit tests cover sanitization (no ARN leakage, fingerprints stable for same input), RBAC/policy enforcement (403 without kms.health.read even for admin), and recommendation mapping. Integration tests validate that known simulated failure modes (AccessDenied, timeout) produce the expected summary. Added a golden response test to prevent accidental schema drift.

Docs/Runbook: Added a short internal note in the on-call admin API docs (restricted). The endpoint is referenced from the KMS dependency degradation runbook, but the runbook PR will be separate to keep this change focused.

Rollout: Feature-flagged behind admin.kmsHealthSummary.enabled (default off). We’ll enable in staging immediately, then in canary prod for on-call only. No customer impact expected. This should help with SUP-18441-type investigations where decrypt failures are intermittent and correlated with throttling/circuit breaker state.

Security considerations: Marcus reviewed the sanitization approach; key fingerprints use a dedicated secret (separate from token signing keys) and are not reusable outside this purpose. Response fields were threat-modeled to avoid turning this into a “key discovery” surface. Access is fully audited with actor + purpose.

Screens/Example response (sanitized): {"tenant_id":"tnt_...","provider":"aws_kms","region":"us-east-1","breaker_state":"half_open","p95_latency_ms_5m":420,"error_rate_5m":0.18,"last_error_class":"Throttling","active_key_fingerprint":"a1b2c3d4e5f6","previous_key_fingerprint":"d4e5f6a1b2c3","recommended_next_steps":["Confirm KMS throttling in provider metrics; consider temporary cache TTL increase per runbook 2.4","If breaker remains half_open >10m, page Security for key policy validation"]} (note: response shown inline is illustrative; actual output does not include free-form error strings).
commits: admin-api: add KMS health summary handler + routing
authz: require kms.health.read permission for health summary endpoint
telemetry: aggregate per-tenant KMS signals (5m/1h windows) + cache
security: implement key fingerprinting + sanitization guards
docs(internal): describe endpoint usage + required purpose param
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we add a metric for endpoint usage (count + latency) so we know if it’s actually helping on-call? Also please confirm we’re not leaking raw provider error messages (they sometimes contain key IDs).

Diego Santos (author): Added admin_api.kms_health_summary.requests + .latency_ms metrics with route + status_code tags. Confirmed we only return error_class enum; removed a leftover field that included error_code string from AWS (could indirectly reveal things). Pushed fixup commit.

Jordan Lee (review): RBAC: please ensure this is not reachable with legacy support_read. We’ve had regressions where “admin” checks were too permissive. Also, do we have a required purpose value for audit trail? That would help GRC later.

Diego Santos (author): Updated middleware to require explicit kms.health.read permission (not implied by support_read). Added required query param purpose with allowlist (incident|support|testing) and emit AUDIT_ADMIN_READ including purpose. Added tests for 400 on missing/invalid purpose.

Marcus Lin (review): Sanitization looks good, but fingerprinting must be HMAC with a dedicated secret and stable across restarts. Please document what secret is used and verify it’s not the JWT signing key. Also ensure response doesn’t include tenant name or external_id.

Diego Santos (author): Implemented HMAC-SHA256 using kms_health_fingerprint_secret (new secret). Confirmed it’s separate from token signing keys. Removed tenant_display_name that was included in an early draft. Added a unit test asserting no tenant name fields.

Sean Gallagher (review): Recommend next steps: can we keep it deterministic and tied to runbook sections? Don’t want free-form guidance that drifts. Also: cache TTL 30s is fine, but make it configurable for incident response.

Diego Santos (author): Mapped recommendations to a fixed table keyed by (error_class, breaker_state). Each recommendation references a runbook section id. Made TTL configurable via admin.kmsHealthSummary.cacheTtlSeconds with safe bounds (10–300s).
Allison Grant (approval): LGTM after metrics addition and removal of raw error fields.
Jordan Lee (approval): LGTM. Thanks for the purpose param + strict permission check.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved with the dedicated secret change; please follow up to ensure secret is provisioned in all envs.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Good to merge. We’ll wire this into the runbook next.
